owner_intent: Mechanicus must distinguish tool discovery, inventory, admission and execution authority.
Existing tools do not become trusted merely because they are present in the repository or were generated by any agent.
Core v1 remains code/script-first. No internal LLM magic may substitute for tool admission evidence.
A future local model membrane may translate Owner intent after Core v1, but it is a deferred capability and cannot admit, execute, land or certify tools.
core_laws: Tool inventory is not tool admission.
Tool admission is not proof of task success.
Read-only admission is not real execution authority.
Dry-run admission is not real execution authority.
Host-bound capability evidence must remain marked host-bound until clean bootstrap or reproducibility proof exists.
No tool receives owner-approved real execution authority in this V2 foundation patch.
Every admitted tool must have identity, purpose, provenance, owner scope, lane binding or explicit lane debt, risk class, execution mode and receipt/report contract.
Rejected or quarantined tools remain visible as evidence debt; they are not silently promoted or hidden.
Custodes may prosecute admission truth; Throne may block global adoption if admission claims exceed evidence.

to_admitted_read_only: tool appears non-mutating by class or contract
to_admitted_dry_run: tool id is allowlisted by Mechanicus command policy for dry-run
to_admitted_owner_approved_execution: requires future Owner approval, sandbox contract, argument schema, real execution allowlist, preflight receipt and post-run receipt
